sections.name: GPU Computing
sections.intro: Tensor APIs, multi-GPU synchronization, and the tools that make GPU experiments easier to run.

cases.title: NumPy-style einsum in MatX
cases.summary: Make tensor expressions easier to write without spelling out every batch dimension.
cases.problem: MatX einsum required explicit output notation and did not support ellipsis notation for batch dimensions.
cases.contribution: Added implicit output inference and ellipsis syntax, with regression tests for both behaviors. Batch dimensions still need matching sizes because of the underlying cuTensorNet constraint.
cases.result: Merged in MatX PR #1224. Expressions such as ...ij,...jk->...ik can now represent matching batch dimensions.

cases.title: Zero-copy mdspan tensor views
cases.summary: Connect modern C++ multidimensional views to MatX tensors.
cases.problem: Using an existing mdspan with MatX needed a direct tensor-view interface, alongside modern multidimensional indexing support.
cases.contribution: Added make_tensor support for cuda::std::mdspan, C++23 tensor[i, j] syntax, documentation, and tests. The PR records passing C++20 tensor tests; C++23 tests required a newer toolchain during review.
cases.result: Merged in MatX PR #1227, enabling views over existing multidimensional data.

cases.title: Independent size and stride widths
cases.summary: Let logical tensor indexes and physical memory offsets use different integer widths.
cases.problem: One 32-bit build switch coupled tensor sizes and memory strides, limiting independent control of their integer widths.
cases.contribution: Introduced separate size and stride build options, retained the legacy switch, and added tests for the four 32-/64-bit combinations.
cases.result: PR #1265 is open. The submission notes that the full test matrix was not completed locally; review and full validation remain outstanding.

cases.title: Safer multi-GPU workspace reuse
cases.summary: Address allocation hangs and stale-buffer risks in matmul_all_reduce.
cases.problem: If one GPU entered allocation while another skipped it, workers could disagree on a collective operation and hang. Repeated calls also need safe buffer reuse.
cases.contribution: Separated allocation from per-call preparation, made allocation decisions collective, and introduced generation-based synchronization with repeated-call GPU tests.
cases.result: Draft PR #581. AMD GPU execution and performance measurements had not been run in the submitted PR, so the fix is presented as work under review.

cases.title: CUDA Neural Network Engine
cases.summary: Understand neural networks from matrix storage to GPU kernel execution.
cases.problem: High-level ML APIs hide the relationship between matrix operations, backpropagation, and compute cost.
cases.contribution: Built matrix operations, dense layers, forward/backpropagation, and a CUDA matrix-multiplication path with correctness tests and CPU/GPU benchmarks.
cases.result: The project reports about 704× speedup for 512×512 multiplication on a Colab Tesla T4 versus its own single-threaded CPU implementation, averaged over five trials. This is a project-specific comparison, not a general library benchmark; CUDA is not yet integrated into the training loop.

cases.title: RunOnGPU
cases.summary: Run a GitHub project on a cloud GPU without rebuilding the setup by hand.
cases.problem: Testing GPU code without local hardware repeatedly involves cloning a repository, configuring Colab, installing dependencies, and running build commands.
cases.contribution: Built a CLI that drives a Colab workflow using setup, build, test, and run commands from a project configuration file.
cases.result: Published on PyPI with doctor, init, and run commands. The documented workflow currently requires Windows, Chrome, and a Google account.

sections.name: AI & ML
sections.intro: Learning systems from the inside out: signals, reproducible pipelines, and agents that act in a browser.

cases.title: Pulse2BP
cases.summary: Build a reproducible pipeline for cuffless blood-pressure estimation from physiological signals.
cases.problem: Long PPG recordings need to be cleaned, segmented, and aligned with arterial blood-pressure targets before they become usable model examples.
cases.contribution: Working with the team on pipeline integration, dataset structure, train/test design, and reproducible evaluation. The workflow covers preprocessing, feature engineering, and modeling.
cases.result: An ongoing AI fellowship project. The repository documents data exploration and preprocessing; no final model-performance result is claimed here.

cases.title: Chexsa
cases.summary: Turn natural-language requests into a sequence of browser actions.
cases.problem: Answering a question and completing a task on a website require different capabilities: an agent must inspect, act, and use feedback.
cases.contribution: Built a modular browser agent around structured tool calls, page context, action history, and error feedback. Windows desktop integration is being developed.
cases.result: The project supports browser navigation and interactions. Desktop control and cross-application workflows remain ongoing work.

cases.title: Learning the math behind the model
cases.summary: Implement the pieces a neural-network framework normally hides.
cases.problem: A framework call can make it hard to see how gradients, weights, and matrix layouts relate.
cases.contribution: Implemented dense-layer gradients, activation functions, gradient-descent updates, and small learning examples in C++.
cases.result: The repository documents regression and XOR learning examples, plus a separate CUDA matrix benchmark. It also lists unfinished features and the next integration steps.

sections.name: Rust
sections.intro: Small tools, close to the system. Exploring Rust by building something I can use.

cases.title: CrabShell
cases.summary: A small terminal for running programs and moving between folders.
cases.problem: A shell is a practical way to explore how command input turns into program execution and directory navigation.
cases.contribution: Built CrabShell in Rust: a simple terminal for typing commands, launching programs, and navigating folders.
cases.result: The public repository contains the project. This page documents CrabShell as a learning project without claiming broader Rust contributions.

sections.name: MLH
sections.intro: MLH Software Engineering Fellow, contributing to Apache Arrow and Parquet through a G-Research-sponsored fellowship.

cases.title: Compression that earns its keep
cases.summary: Let writers skip compression when its storage savings are too small to justify the work.
cases.problem: Parquet V2 pages could keep compressed values even when they were only slightly smaller than the original data.
cases.contribution: Added a configurable min_space_savings threshold in C++ and Python, preserved default behavior, and added unit tests for both implementations.
cases.result: Draft PR #52580 is open. The setting lets a value such as 0.1 require at least 10% savings before keeping compressed values. The earlier #52579 submission is closed and shown in the submission history below.

cases.title: Fixed-size-list fast paths
cases.summary: Explore less overhead when list sizes are known ahead of time.
cases.problem: Reader and writer paths for fixed-size lists can spend work handling definition and repetition levels that may be avoidable in specialized paths.
cases.contribution: Developing fixed-size-list reader/writer fast paths as part of my Arrow work.
cases.result: Ongoing work described in my résumé. A public PR and measured performance result are not linked yet.

sections.name: Projects
sections.alt: Silver and lavender developer folder sculpture
sections.intro: Applications and tools that turn a recurring problem into something usable.

cases.title: CampCrunch
cases.summary: A mobile application backed by university dining-hall data.
cases.problem: The application needed reliable dining-data ingestion and dashboard access patterns that would not overload the backend.
cases.contribution: Built the database and ingestion pipeline, redesigned queries and dashboard data access, and led a four-developer team through reviews and delivery.
cases.result: Reduced backend query load by 40%, as reported in my résumé, while supporting beta users. The repository provides the code; it does not provide a public production dashboard.

cases.title: RunOnGPU
cases.summary: A repeatable route from a GitHub repository to a Colab GPU run.
cases.problem: Getting GPU experiments running required the same manual setup steps each time.
cases.contribution: Built a configurable CLI workflow for cloning, environment setup, builds, tests, and execution.
cases.result: Published on PyPI, with documented setup checks and examples.

cases.title: Chexsa
cases.summary: An agent that interacts with websites through structured actions.
cases.problem: Useful automation needs to interpret a page and respond to what happened after each action.
cases.contribution: Built browser tools and an agent loop using page context, execution history, and error feedback.
cases.result: Browser workflows are implemented; Windows desktop integration remains under development.

sections.name: Research
sections.alt: White and violet laboratory microscope sculpture
sections.intro: Where software meets experiments: computer vision, hardware automation, and polymer research.

cases.title: Automating contact-angle measurement
cases.org: Arizona State University · System integration internship
cases.summary: Connect image analysis to experimental hardware and data processing.
cases.problem: Manual contact-angle analysis and experiment handling limit the throughput of a measurement workflow.
cases.contribution: Developed a computer-vision pipeline and embedded hardware automation for measurement and data processing.
cases.result: My résumé reports over 80% measurement accuracy and a threefold increase in experimental throughput. These results are résumé-reported; the project code is not publicly shared.

cases.title: High-throughput polymer development
cases.summary: A review of how high-throughput experiments and machine learning can accelerate polymer development.
cases.problem: Exploring large polymer design spaces requires high-quality data and faster experimental and analytical workflows.
cases.contribution: Co-authored the review, “Convergence of high throughput experimentation and machine learning to rapidly advance application-specific polymer development.”
cases.result: Published May 28, 2026 in RSC Applied Polymers. This publication is presented separately from my ASU internship.
